entities.summary:
Drest VIII was the son of Talorcan and became king of the Picts in 782 CE, succeeding his father Talorgan. He reigned until his death in 783 CE.

As king, Drest VIII played a crucial role in maintaining the stability of the Pictish kingdom during a time of political turmoil in Scotland. His reign was marked by several significant events, including the construction of new fortifications and the strengthening of alliances with neighboring kingdoms.

Despite his efforts to maintain peace, Drest VIII's rule was cut short when he died suddenly in 783 CE. This event had a profound impact on the Pictish kingdom, leading to a period of instability and power struggles among the various factions vying for control.

The legacy of Drest VIII can be seen in the many historical accounts that describe his reign as a time of relative peace and prosperity for the Picts. However, it is also worth noting that the details of his life and reign are not always well-documented, leaving room for interpretation and speculation among historians.

In the words of the 9th-century Scottish historian Adamnan, 'Drest VIII was a king who ruled with wisdom and justice, but whose life was cut short by the hand of fate.'
